guides.title: Plan a career change with Claude + Scout
guides.blurb: A step-by-step way to find what from your background already counts in your new field, spot the real gaps, and explain your switch in one clear sentence.
inside: How to turn your old job titles into proof the new field understands
A prompt that matches your skills to real job postings
A one-sentence switch story you can use anywhere
How to get a full skill-gap plan from Claude with Scout
How to close each gap without skipping what the field requires
Where to put your switch story so people get it fast
guides.intro:
You want to switch careers, but on paper your experience doesn't seem to line up. So you shrink it. You list old job titles, hope someone connects the dots, and wait. Most people never do. That's not because you aren't qualified. It's because your best work is hiding in language the new field doesn't recognize, and the jump hasn't been explained in a way that clicks.

This guide fixes both. First you'll pull the transferable proof out of your background and translate it into your new field's words. Then you'll write the one sentence that explains your switch. The first three steps work with any AI chat, no extra tools. After that, you'll see how Scout in Claude can build the whole skill-gap plan for you in one go. You've done real work. Let's make it easy to see.

free.body:
Job titles don't travel well between fields. What you actually did does. Grab a blank page and write down the tasks you handled, the problems you solved, and the things that changed because you were there.

Think about people you helped, processes you fixed, numbers you tracked, tools you learned, and moments someone came to you for help. Write them as plain actions, like "trained new hires" or "cut down customer complaints by changing the follow-up process." Only use real numbers you actually know. If you don't know an exact number, just describe what happened.

Don't filter yet. Small things count. This list is the raw material for everything that follows.
free.prompt: I'm planning a career change and I want to list everything I've actually done, not just my job titles. Here's my background: [paste your roles, a few lines about each one, and anything you're proud of]. Ask me up to 8 short questions to pull out tasks, problems I solved, tools I used, and results I can honestly describe. Then give me a clean bullet list of my work written as plain actions. Don't invent any numbers or results. If something needs a detail only I know, mark it with [add detail].
free.title: Step 1: List what you did, not what you were called

free.body:
Now find 3 to 5 real job postings in the field you want. Pick roles you could realistically go for next, not the dream role five steps up. Copy the duties and requirements sections.

Put your list from Step 1 side by side with those postings. You're looking for overlap. A teacher who "planned lessons for different learning levels" may be doing what an instructional designer calls "designing content for varied audiences." Same skill, different words.

This step also shows you what's missing. That's good news. A clear gap is something you can work on. A vague feeling of "I'm not enough" isn't.
free.prompt: I want to move into [new field / target role]. Here is my list of past work: [paste your list from Step 1]. Here are job postings I'm aiming for: [paste 3 to 5 postings]. Please do three things. 1) Match each item from my work to the posting requirements it supports, and rewrite it in the language this field uses. Keep it honest and don't stretch what I did. 2) List the requirements I don't clearly show yet, and say which ones look required (like a license, certification, or degree) versus nice to have. 3) Tell me which of my strengths show up most across these postings.
free.title: Step 2: Translate your work into your new field's language

free.body:
When someone asks "so why the change?" you want a calm, clear answer, not a long apology. A good switch story connects three things: what you've been doing, the thread that carries over, and why the new field is the natural next step.

A simple shape: "I've spent [time] doing [old work], where I kept [the transferable thing], and I'm moving into [new field] to [what you want to do there]." Keep it to one sentence you could say out loud without notes.

Write a few versions, read them aloud, and keep the one that sounds like you on a good day.
free.prompt: Help me explain my career change in one sentence. My background: [your old field and roles]. The new field: [new field / target role]. The strongest skills that carry over: [paste the top matches from Step 2]. Why I want this switch: [your honest reason]. Write 5 one-sentence versions that connect my past work to the new role. Keep them plain, confident, and under 35 words each. No buzzwords, no apologizing for the change, and don't claim experience I don't have. Then tell me which one is clearest and why.
free.title: Step 3: Write your switch story in one sentence

locked.body:
The free steps work, but they take a few rounds of copying and pasting. Scout is a job search helper you can add to Claude so it does the transfer check, the gap list, and the switch story together in one chat.

On your computer, open this link and follow the setup: https://scoutjob.ai/start?app=claude&ref=hireme-hub&utm_source=hireme&utm_medium=creator-hub&utm_campaign=plan-a-career-change&utm_content=aleah

One honest note: Scout is free for 7 days with a card, then $97/month. So pick the field you're most serious about before you start, and have your background handy.
locked.title: Step 4: Add Scout to Claude

locked.body:
Open a new chat in Claude and paste the prompt below. Swap in the field you want to move into. If Scout asks for your resume or background, share it. The more real detail it has, the more useful the plan.

What you'll see is a skill-gap plan with four parts: the transferable proof from your background, the real gaps, the fastest way to close each one, and your switch story.

Compare it to what you wrote in Steps 2 and 3. Keep what's strongest from each. You know your own history best, so fix anything that doesn't sound true to you.
locked.prompt: Scout, I want to move into [new field]. What from my background transfers, what's missing, and how do I explain the switch?
locked.title: Step 5: Ask Scout for your skill-gap plan

locked.body:
Take your list of gaps and sort it into two groups. Group one is anything the field actually requires, like a license, certification, or specific degree. Those are not optional, and no story replaces them. Check the requirement with the licensing body or the official source for your field, then put it on your plan with real next steps.

Group two is everything else: a tool you haven't used, a type of project you haven't done, vocabulary you're still learning. These are often faster to close with a short course, a small practice project, volunteer work, or taking on a related task in your current job.

For each gap, write one next action you can start this week. Small and specific beats big and vague.
locked.prompt: Here are the gaps between my background and [new field]: [paste the gaps from Scout or Step 2]. For each one, tell me: 1) whether it's typically a firm requirement in this field (license, certification, degree) or a skill I can build, and where I should confirm that, 2) the fastest realistic way to start closing it, and 3) one concrete action I can take this week. Don't suggest skipping anything the field requires. Keep it simple and practical.
locked.title: Step 6: Close each gap the honest way

locked.body:
Your one sentence only helps if people read it. Use it at the top of your resume summary, in your LinkedIn headline or About section, in the first lines of cover letters, and as your answer to "tell me about yourself."

Then lead your resume bullets with the translated proof from Step 2 or Scout's plan, using the new field's words. Someone skimming should see the connection in seconds without having to guess.

You're not hiding the switch. You're making it obvious why it makes sense.
locked.prompt: Here is my switch story: [paste your one sentence]. Here is my translated proof: [paste your strongest matched bullets]. My target role: [new field / role]. Please write: 1) a 3-line resume summary, 2) a LinkedIn headline under 200 characters, 3) a short LinkedIn About section, and 4) a 30-second spoken answer to "tell me about yourself." Keep everything honest, plain, and consistent with my story. Don't add experience or results I haven't given you.
locked.title: Step 7: Put your switch story where people will see it

guides.tip: Say your switch story out loud to one friend who doesn't work in your new field. If they can repeat the gist back to you in their own words, it's ready. If they look confused, cut a clause and try again.

guides.title: Find your next career path with Claude + Scout
guides.blurb: By the end, you'll have 2 to 3 roles next to your current one, the proof from your own experience for each, and one clear gap to close for each.
inside: Have Scout do it for you
guides.intro: If you don't know which job to go for, it's easy to apply to everything. That's not a flaw in you. It's what happens when nothing feels like a clear fit. The trouble is that a scattered search can look unfocused to the person reading it. Picking a few roles on purpose gives your search a clear direction.

free.title: Step 1: Do it yourself in 15 minutes
free.body:
You can do this with any AI chat, like ChatGPT or Claude. No Scout needed.

1. Gather your material (3 minutes). Open your current resume. Also jot down a few things you're proud of at work, even small ones. Keep it all in one place.

2. Paste in your experience (2 minutes). Open a new chat and paste this. Then paste your resume right below it.

3. Ask for adjacent roles (3 minutes). Paste this:

4. Check the evidence (3 minutes). Read each answer. Does the evidence really come from your resume? If something looks off, push back:

5. Look at the gaps (2 minutes). Paste this:

6. Pick one to test (2 minutes). Choose the role that excites you most and where the gap feels doable. Then ask:

Save your answers in a note. Now your search has a direction.
free.prompt:
I'm going to share my resume. Please read it closely and wait. Don't suggest anything yet. When you're done, reply only with: "Ready for your next question."

Based on my resume, which roles fit my experience that I haven't considered? Give me 2 to 3 roles that are close to what I already do. For each role, tell me: (1) why it fits, using specific evidence from my resume, and (2) the biggest gap between my experience and that role. Keep it plain and short. Don't guess at pay.

For each role, quote the exact line or detail from my resume that supports it. If you can't find one, say so and remove the role.

For each role, what is one small, realistic thing I could do in the next 30 days to start closing the gap? Examples: a short course, a project, a conversation with someone in that role, or a change to how I describe my work.

Rewrite my resume summary so it speaks to this role. Use only what's true in my resume. Don't add skills or experience I don't have.

locked.prompt: Scout, which roles fit my experience that I haven't considered?

guides.tip: Don't try to pick your forever job. Just pick one role to test this week. Take the role from your list with the smallest gap, then look at 5 real job posts for it. Highlight every line you could already speak to from your own work. If most of the lines feel familiar, you've got a good lead. If few do, cross it off and try the next one. You're qualified. Now give your search a clear target.
